- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and forecast is overly optimistic, lower the 30d mean by 2–5% to reflect bearish bias.  
- After a recent price spike (last 3–5 days > 73), model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast to allow 1–2% lagged continuation.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 1.0, 0.3, 1.0), model overfits short-term momentum — dampen forecast volatility by 10–15% in next 5–7 days.  
- When true outcome is consistently below forecast (e.g., 3–5% gap over 10+ days), apply mean reversion: reduce forecast by 1–3% per day until convergence to recent 10-day average.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.7) and forecast is flat, model underreacts — increase forecast by 1–2% to capture latent market sentiment.
